angle: Why does Britain love a painting of a war hero being towed to the scrapyard?
answer: Because Turner turned a routine tow into a funeral for the age of sail: he restored the stripped masts, painted the old ship as a pale ghost behind a dark smoking tug, set the sun on one side and a new moon on the other, and then refused to sell it, leaving it to the nation.
